note_claims.claim: The patient has had a cough and coryza for 4 days.
The patient has had increased work of breathing since yesterday.
The patient has had a temperature up to 37.9 °C.
The patient has had feeding about half his usual amount since yesterday.
The patient has had four wet nappies in 24 hours.
The patient has no history of apnoea (older sister had an apnoea with bronchiolitis two years ago).
The patient has no history of cardiac or respiratory problems.
The patient's immunisations are up to date.
The patient has taken Calpol once yesterday.
The patient has no known drug allergies.
The patient's temperature is 37.8 °C.
The patient's respiratory rate is 54 times a minute.
The patient's heart rate is 150.
The patient's oxygen level is 95 percent in air.
The patient exhibits intercostal and subcostal recession when breathing.
The patient's capillary refill is under two seconds.
The patient is alert and looking around.
The clinical impression is Bronchiolitis with increased work of breathing (intercostal recession) and feeds about 50% of usual.
The plan is a same-day referral to the paediatric assessment unit.
The plan is to give the patient small, frequent feeds and saline nose drops before feeds.
The patient is advised that the illness may worsen over days 3–5.
The safety-netting advice is to call 999 if there are pauses in breathing, blue colour, or severe difficulty breathing on the way.
The safety-netting advice is to call the practice back if unable to attend within the hour to arrange an ambulance.

transcript_facts.fact: Arlo has had a runny nose and a cough for four days.
Arlo's breathing has been going really fast since yesterday.
Arlo is seven months old.
Arlo had a temperature of 37.9 °C this morning.
Arlo was initially reported as taking most of his bottles.
Arlo is only managing about half of each bottle since yesterday.
The father did the night feeds.
Arlo keeps pulling off to breathe.
Arlo had four wet nappies in the last 24 hours.
Arlo usually has six or seven wet nappies.
Arlo's sister had an apnoea with bronchiolitis two years ago.
There was no history of apnoea with Arlo.
Arlo has not gone blue or very pale.
Arlo brought up a bit of milk after coughing.
Arlo was born at 39 weeks.
Arlo has no heart or lung problems.
Arlo's immunisations are up to date.
Arlo has taken Calpol once yesterday.
The father smokes, but only outside, never in the house.
Arlo's temperature is 37.8 °C.
Arlo's respiratory rate is 54 times a minute.
Arlo's heart rate is 150.
Arlo's oxygen level is 95 percent.
Arlo is pulling in between his ribs and under them when he breathes.
Arlo's capillary refill is under two seconds.
Arlo is alert and looking around.
Arlo has bilateral fine crackles and wheeze on both sides of his chest.
Arlo is working hard to breathe, with that pulling in between his ribs.
Arlo's feeding is down to about half.
The clinician recommends seeing Arlo at the hospital today.
The clinician will ring the paediatric team.
The paediatric team can keep an eye on his breathing, help with feeds, and give him oxygen or other treatment if needed.
The clinician advises giving Arlo smaller feeds more often until he gets there.
The clinician advises saline drops in his nose before feeds to help clear it.
Bronchiolitis often gets worse over the first three to five days before it gets better.
If on the way, the patient should call 999 if he has any pauses in his breathing, goes blue, or is really struggling to breathe.
If the patient cannot get there within the hour, they should ring back and an ambulance will be arranged.
